messages.subject: Curving transects
parts:
Dear List,

To make a long story short- I have attempted to use standard line transect
sampling techniques on curving trails to estimate the density of hornbills.
In theory we were supposed to estimate the shortest distance between
the birds and the curving transect, however it was not possible to
accurately estimate
this distance in such dense forest & rugged terrain where most
of the detections were aural often at distances well over 100 m .
My question is how badly biased will such results be
and in what direction if I conduct the analysis assuming the transects were
straight, when they clearly were not. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.
